sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Explicit vs. Implicit
sections.content: Briefly contrast explicit functions (y=f(x)) with implicit relations (where y is 'tangled' with x). Use a visual analogy: a 'neatly folded shirt' (explicit) vs. a 'tangled ball of yarn' (implicit). Recall the Chain Rule: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x).
sections.example: Explicit: y=x^2. Implicit: x^2 + y^2 = 25 (the equation of a circle).

sections.title: The 'Secret Sauce': The Chain Rule for y
sections.content: Introduce the core mechanic: whenever we differentiate a term containing 'y' with respect to 'x', we must multiply by dy/dx. Visualize 'y' as a hidden function 'y(x)' inside the expression.
sections.example: Differentiating y^3: Treat as (y)^3. Derivative is 3y^2 * (dy/dx).

sections.title: Step-by-Step Execution: The Squirrel Problem
sections.content: Demonstrate the algorithm: 1. Differentiate both sides with respect to x. 2. Collect all dy/dx terms on one side. 3. Factor out dy/dx and solve. Use a graphical animation of a squirrel running along the curve x^2 + y^2 = 25 to show the changing slope.
sections.example: Find dy/dx for x^2 + y^2 = 25. Step 1: 2x + 2y(dy/dx) = 0. Step 2: 2y(dy/dx) = -2x. Result: dy/dx = -x/y.

sections.title: Visualizing the Tangent Line
sections.content: Connect the algebraic result to geometry. Show how the calculated dy/dx gives the slope of the tangent line at any point (x, y) on the implicit curve. Emphasize that the slope depends on both x and y coordinates.
sections.example: At point (3, 4) on the circle, the slope is dy/dx = -3/4. The tangent line drops 3 units for every 4 units across.

sections.title: Summary & Pro-Tips
sections.content: Quick recap: Always apply the Chain Rule to 'y' terms; keep terms with dy/dx on the left and move constants/x-terms to the right. A final visual 'Checklist' pops up on screen to reinforce the workflow.
sections.example: Common pitfall: Forgetting to multiply by dy/dx when differentiating y. Remember: 'If you see a y, append a dy/dx!'
